subject: docs/coop/artifacts/platform-tcb-contract.v6.json

blockers.title: linux-distro-userspace names the missing discriminator but does not define a closed canonical identifier
evidence: The new observation is only prose: 'publisher/distribution identifier plus userspace-release'. It defines no component fields, authoritative source, publisher/distribution namespace, normalization, delimiter or structured serialization. EXACT-BUILD nevertheless compares one canonicalIdentifier 'after normalization', but no Linux normalization exists.

The alternative '(or equivalent PLATFORM-ATTESTED platform-image identity)' is an open second form with no selector tag, attestation-scheme identifier, payload shape, canonicalization, or equality rule. PLATFORM-ATTESTED elsewhere describes object authenticity through codesign, package db, or equivalent; it does not define a platform-profile canonicalIdentifier.

The later packet may choose values but is forbidden to mint scheme semantics. It would therefore have to invent whether the Linux identifier is a tuple, concatenated string, or attestation object and how equivalent observed values compare.
blockers.impact: Conforming producers can encode the same Linux host differently or conflate distinct publisher/release pairs, so a frozen allowlist and its G22 qualification cannot share one reproducible complete profile key.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define linux-distro-userspace as a closed, versioned tagged payload with exact fields, authoritative observation sources, per-field normalization, unambiguous serialization, and equality. If an attested-image alternative is retained, give it its own tag plus a closed attestation-scheme registry and identity payload; otherwise remove the open alternative. The packet must only populate these defined fields.

blockers.title: OTHER-FSTYPE still lacks one deterministic per-platform observation algorithm
evidence: tokenSource selects 'statfs/f_fstypename (or equivalent)' rather than one named, versioned source per osFamily. The slash and open equivalent clause permit different interfaces and token vocabularies for the same filesystem; no mapping chooses among them.

lawfulOnlyWhen tests whether the 'platform-reported' type is absent from identifierEnum, while normalization separately applies ASCII case-fold. The contract does not say whether normalization precedes the enum-absence test. A token such as EXT4 can therefore become enum ext4 under one reader or OTHER-FSTYPE under another.
The exact serialization and digest format close the output object but cannot repair disagreement about which source token and branch must produce it.
blockers.impact: The same host filesystem can occupy different required-member values across conforming verifiers, making the complete profile key and signed allowlist non-reproducible.
blockers.requiredRepair: For each osFamily, name one exact observation API/field or a versioned mapping algorithm, including the filesystem/mount being measured and failure behavior. Remove the 'or equivalent' escape, state that normalization occurs before enum lookup, and use OTHER-FSTYPE only when that normalized token is absent.

shouldFix.title: Encoding sonameAbi deleted the predecessor's non-identity comparison rule
shouldFix.evidence: V6 adds the named sonameAbi field but removes v5's explicit rule that companion labels never decide identity and authenticity remains the attested or digest-bound object. The replacement says only notAuthenticity and never sole authenticity. Because sameMeans compares identityEvidence and sonameAbi now resides inside that payload, the contract no longer says whether a missing or mismatched companion is ignored for identity, causes identity drift, or is checked separately as compatibility.
shouldFix.impact: Two verifiers can reach different allow/refuse outcomes for the same authenticated libc object and companion labels. The field encoding is now closed, but its comparison semantics are not.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restore an explicit rule for presence, absence, and mismatch of sonameAbi. If it is metadata only, exclude it from identity equality; if it gates compatibility, define that separate comparison and refusal outcome while preserving PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND as the authenticity identity.

measurements.check: Closed Linux publisher/distribution and userspace selector
measurements.evidence: Scheme-to-osFamily binding landed and uname release was removed, but linux-distro-userspace has no structured canonicalIdentifier grammar and retains an open attestation alternative. See PTCB-V6-B1.

measurements.check: Deterministic OTHER-FSTYPE observation and enum branching
measurements.evidence: The digest object is structured, but its source remains statfs/f_fstypename/or-equivalent and enum absence is not ordered after normalization. See PTCB-V6-B2.
The optional payload field is now encoded in both lawful libc authenticity tags, but v5's non-identity comparison rule was removed without replacement. See PTCB-V6-S1.

macos-product-build and linux-distro-userspace are now explicitly bound to their osFamily, uname-release alone is removed, EXACT-BUILD retains exact scheme-aware equality, and CLOSED-RANGE remains prohibited. PTCB-V6-B1 concerns the still-open Linux canonical payload, not these landed constraints.

OTHER-FSTYPE now declares NFC and ASCII case-fold, sha-256, 64 lowercase hex, enum absence, and exact {tag, algorithmId, digest} serialization. PTCB-V6-B2 concerns source selection and branch ordering, not output encoding.

Both lawful libc authenticity payloads expose the same optional sonameAbi field and reject extra forms. SONAME-ABI is absent from classMap and cannot be a fifth signed field or sole authenticity. PTCB-V6-S1 concerns the removed comparison rule.

measurements.check: Exhaustive signed entry and declared-versus-ambient predicate
measurements.evidence: identityRuleShape.declared and signedEntry.required agree on exactly four exhaustive fields. environmentInfluence is a closed FIXED/FORBIDDEN map; unnamed influence and mutable PATH/loader substitution refuse.

The observation boundary covers every actual attempt, capture is independent of the tested process, lifecycle and sensor-health closure are required, retained events bind subject/profile/carrier/process/class/outcome, and false-match use fails.

measurements.check: One carrier, population reservation, and carrier-absence consequence
measurements.evidence: One DR-101 successor owns exactly one inventory copy; DR-103 consumes it; ceremony is separate; and G22 cannot QUALIFY without it. All selector members and per-OS TCB members remain RESERVED, and no later packet or owner is designated.

The subject binds NOTHING, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and DO-NOT-SEAL, leaves DR-126 OPEN, excludes language-runtime/Node from the core taxonomy, re-owns neither DR-G07 nor D-006 numbers, creates no D-096 (A) grant, and authorizes no implementation.

attacks.attack: linux-distro-userspace is a closed canonical key rather than renamed packet-defined prose
attacks.evidence: The osFamily binding is explicit, but the Linux component/source/serialization grammar and attested alternative remain undefined. See PTCB-V6-B1.

attacks.attack: OTHER-FSTYPE has one named source, a deterministic case rule, and an unambiguous enum-absent condition
attacks.evidence: Case normalization and enum absence are named, but interface choice remains open and their evaluation order is unspecified. See PTCB-V6-B2.

attacks.attack: sonameAbi is both encodable and comparison-closed inside libc authenticity payloads
attacks.evidence: Encoding landed, but removal of the predecessor's 'never decide identity' rule makes mismatch behavior indeterminate. See PTCB-V6-S1.

attacks.attack: A scheme can cross osFamily, uname release alone survives, or CLOSED-RANGE occupies the required member
attacks.evidence: Scheme binding is explicit, the uname-only scheme is removed, and CLOSED-RANGE is prohibited.

attacks.attack: SONAME-ABI becomes a fifth field or sole libc authenticity
attacks.evidence: sonameAbi is nested in both lawful authenticity payloads, extra forms are rejected, and classMap permits only PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND for libc.

attacks.attack: A three-field entry survives or naming PATH/loader influence makes mutable substitution lawful
attacks.evidence: The declared and detailed shapes agree on four exhaustive fields, while environment influence accepts only fixed signed values or refusal.

attacks.attack: Capture can self-assert completeness, omit actual attempts, or use a false evidence join
attacks.evidence: Independent capture, lifecycle/sensor-health closure, independently checkable inapplicability proof, retained bindings, and false-match failure remain mandatory.

attacks.attack: Carrier ownership is joint or absent without blocking G22
attacks.evidence: Field authorship remains singular, consumers and ceremony are separate, and absence expressly prevents qualification.

attacks.attack: The v5-to-v6 path contains an unrostered semantic change
attacks.evidence: All 29 changed semantic nodes are rostered or succession metadata; review guidance is append-only and the inherited-live-locator edit is expressly named.

attacks.attack: The candidate populates platform tables, designates a later packet, expands the core TCB, satisfies DR-126, qualifies G22, or grants application/implementation authority
attacks.evidence: Selectors and members remain RESERVED, the packet is indefinite, scope remains narrow, DR-126 remains OPEN, G22 remains unqualified, and every application or implementation claim is denied.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. The Linux selector still has no closed canonical payload, OTHER-FSTYPE still has no single deterministic observation algorithm, and sonameAbi lost its predecessor's comparison rule. DR-126 remains OPEN; no D-096 (A) grant, satisfaction, qualification, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
